_comment: Reference list for MANUAL cross-checks only: codes documented to support checkpoint/restart, with the mechanism and where it is documented. It is NOT used to flag entries or in any computation (the analysis is code-agnostic); hpc_analysis.restart_cross_check() lists matches when a committee member asks. Compiled 2026-10 from the codes' documentation; 'reference_type' says whether the reference is the code's own documentation ('official') or a secondary source still to verify ('secondary'); all are official as of 2026-10-26, and 'verified' records when an entry was checked against its manual. Support can depend on version, calculation type and settings (e.g. whether restart files were written before the job stopped). Matching is case-insensitive on the code name with spaces and punctuation removed; 'aliases' map other names.

quantumespresso.name: Quantum ESPRESSO (pw.x)
quantumespresso.mechanism: restart_mode='restart'; the earlier run must stop cleanly via max_seconds or a prefix.EXIT file, otherwise no clean restart

vasp.name: VASP
vasp.mechanism: ISTART=1/2 reads orbitals from WAVECAR (falls back to a fresh start if WAVECAR is missing or does not match); CONTCAR for positions

gromacs.name: GROMACS
gromacs.mechanism: gmx mdrun writes .cpt checkpoints (interval -cpt) and continues exactly with -cpi; -maxh stops cleanly before the wall-time limit

lammps.name: LAMMPS
lammps.mechanism: restart N / write_restart write binary restart files; read_restart continues (fixes must be re-specified in the input)

cp2k.name: CP2K
cp2k.mechanism: EXT_RESTART section reads the .restart file written during the run; wavefunctions via WFN_RESTART_FILE_NAME

namd.name: NAMD
namd.mechanism: restartname + restartfreq write restart coordinates/velocities; continue with bincoordinates, binvelocities and extendedSystem

amber.name: Amber (sander / pmemd)
amber.mechanism: restart file written every ntwr steps; continue with irest=1, ntx=5 (MD only; a minimisation restart has no velocities)
amber.notes: Reference is an official Amber tutorial; the variable definitions are in the Amber manual for the version used.

openfoam.name: OpenFOAM
openfoam.mechanism: time directories written per writeControl/writeInterval in controlDict; startFrom latestTime continues from the newest

wrf.name: WRF
wrf.mechanism: restart_interval (minutes) writes wrfrst files; continue with restart=.true. and new start time (no need to rerun WPS/real.exe)

octopus.name: Octopus
octopus.mechanism: restart data (e.g. wavefunctions) written to restart directories; RestartOptions controls reading them

gpaw.name: GPAW
gpaw.mechanism: .gpw restart files (calc.write, or calc.attach for every n SCF steps); restart with GPAW('file.gpw')

nwchem.name: NWChem
nwchem.mechanism: RESTART directive reuses the run database (file_prefix.db) and its files, keeping the same file prefix; list only the unfinished tasks after it. Recommended when a job runs out of queue time

siesta.name: SIESTA
siesta.mechanism: positions and velocities saved to SystemLabel.XV every step (MD.UseSaveXV reads them); seamless MD continuation via SystemLabel.VERLET_RESTART / NOSE_RESTART / PR_RESTART / NPR_RESTART / ANNEAL_RESTART; DM.UseSaveDM (default true) reads the saved density matrix
siesta.notes: Without the *_RESTART file, MD 'restarts' by repeating the last step from XV, which the manual says is not a seamless continuation.

abinit.name: ABINIT
abinit.mechanism: restartxf = -1/-2/-3 restarts MD or structural optimisation from the HIST.nc file written every iteration (also for unfinished runs; only predictors without random numbers); irdwfk=1 / getwfk read earlier _WFK wavefunctions
abinit.notes: Positive restartxf values are deprecated since ABINIT v8 (older forum advice to use restartxf 1 no longer applies).

dlpoly.name: DL_POLY
dlpoly.mechanism: REVCON (configuration) and REVIVE (statistics) written every ndump steps; rename to CONFIG and REVOLD and add 'restart' to CONTROL
dlpoly.notes: Copy of the DL_POLY 2 user manual; DL_POLY 4/5 file names may differ.

cpmd.name: CPMD
cpmd.mechanism: RESTART [options] in &CPMD reads the binary RESTART file (MD: WAVEFUNCTION COORDINATES VELOCITIES, plus ACCUMULATORS and Nose options if used; LATEST reads the newest). Written at the end and at intervals set by STORE; RESTFILE keeps several
cpmd.notes: The CPMD consortium's manual for CPMD 4.3.0 (6 March 2024), section 11.7 'Restarts' and keyword RESTART; this link is a copy hosted by the University of Calgary (project site: http://www.cpmd.org/).

castep.name: CASTEP
castep.mechanism: checkpoint written to seedname.check; continue with CONTINUATION (only some parameters may change)
